sentences.text:
Sreemani B Kurup K.P.. vs Special Tahsildar (La) on 16 March,
2023
Bench: Surya Kant, J.K. Maheshwari

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal No.2687/2011
 Sreemani B Kurup K.P. & Ors. 
 Versus
 Special Tahsildar (La) & Anr. 
 O R D E R
The appellants, being dissatisfied with the amount of compensation awarded to them for their acquired land by the Kerala High Court vide impugned Judgment dated 03062010, are in appeal before us.

2. The undisputed facts are that the State of Kerala issued a Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter, the Act) on 10042005 proposing to acquire land for widening of the National Highway by National Highway Authority running from Kozhikode to Kannur.
The properties sought to be acquired were situated within the limits of Vadakara Municipal Town.
The land of the appellants measuring 35.065 cents was eventually acquired as a part of this public purpose.
The Land Acquisition Officer passed an Award on 10052007 granting compensation of Rs. 22,290.66/ per cent.
The appellants filed Reference under Section 18 of the Act.

The Reference Court obtained a Report evaluating the entire evidence on record, it awarded compensation of Rs.37,500/ per cent vide Award dated 20122008.
3.

The appellants remained dissatisfied and proceeded to approach the High Court and vide the impugned judgment, their First Appeal was allowed in part to the extent that the High Court has granted compensation of Rs.45,000/ per cent.
4. The short question that falls for our consideration is whether the appellants are entitled to compensation at a rate higher than Rs.45,000/ per cent?
5. We have heard Mr. A. Hari Prasad, learned Senior Counsel on behalf of the appellants and learned counsel on behalf of the State of Kerala and perused the entire material on record.

6. There are two examplars Exhibit `A1 and Exhibit `A2, which are stated to be purchases of Sreemani B Kurup K.P.. vs Special Tahsildar (La) on 16 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75635994/
1 similar pieces of land, and are being heavily relied upon by the appellants to urge that they are entitled to compensation at a rate higher than what has been awarded by the High Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Exhibit `A1 is a copy of the Registered Sale Deed dated 19032002 whereby Reliance purchased a piece of land admeasuring 12 cents for a total sale consideration of Rs.9,00,000/, i.e., at Rs.75,000/ per cent.

Exhibit `A2 is a certified copy of the Judgment of the Reference Court in LAR 8/2005 dated 20122006 whereby compensation of Rs.50,000/ per cent has been awarded, in respect of the land for which the acquisition process had been initiated vide Notification dated 16122002,
issued under Section 4 of the Act for acquiring properties for the same purpose, namely, the widening of the subject National Highway.
7. Both these earlier instances (Exhibit `A1 & `A2) have been discussed in extenso by the Reference Court and have been rejected.

While Exhibit `A1 has been discarded on the ground that the sale consideration in that instance was not determinative of the actual market value as big companies like Reliance offer hefty prices for installation of their mobile phone towers, keeping in view the need for specific locations for such installations.
The Award Exhibit `A2 has not been relied upon on the premise that the land acquired therein was not far away from Karimpanappalam, Vadakara New Bus Stand and Narayana Nagaram Junction.

It has also been pointed out that in the case of Exhibit `A2, the Land Acquisition Officer had given compensation of Rs.28,888/ whereas for the acquired properties in the case in hand, only Rs.22,291/ per cent was awarded.

8. The appellants cited both the abovementioned instances in appeal before the High Court but could not persuade the High Court to rely upon them as may be seen from the following observations: Very strong reliance was placed before the court below on Ext. A2 common judgment in respect of a batch of ten cases relating to acquisition for the same purpose, but pursuant to Section 4(1) notification, some three years earlier.

The Advocate Commissioner in his report Ext.X1 reported that the property in one of the cases covered by Ext.A2 is situated just opposite to the property in one of the cases covered by the batch of cases covered by the impugned judgment.
Nevertheless, the learned Subordinate Judge took a view that Ext.A2 properties are situated far away from the properties under Acquisition and hence the value fixed under Ext.A2 cannot be granted.

For Ext.A2 properties, even three years earlier to the present notification, the Land Acquisition Officer had awarded value of Rs.28,888/ which is more than the value of Rs.22,000/ awarded for the present property three years subsequently.

The argument of Mr.
M.Gopikrishnari Nambiar under the finding that Ext.A2 properties are situate far away from the town
is not correct.
We feel that Ext.A2 properties were slightly superior in quality.
At the same time, taking all relevant aspects into account including Ext.A2, according to us the value of the land under acquisition can be fixed at Rs.45,000/ per cent.
It is accordingly fixed.

9. Learned Senior Counsel for the appellants has reiterated their reliance on Exhibit `A1 and Exhibit `A2 contending, inter alia, that the land in both those cases were also located within the same municipal area/town where the appellants acquired land was situated.
He submits that the distance between the land acquired vide Exhibit `A2 and the land of the appellants is also not far away.

According to him, the sale instance at Exhibit `A1 is equally relevant, as the land there was acquired in a residential area, whereas the land of the appellants admittedly has commercial potentiality, given that it adjoined the National Highway.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the State of Kerala, on the other hand, heavily relies upon the concurrent findings of fact returned by the Reference Court and the High Court to urge that lands in Exhibit `A1 and Exhibit `A2, respectively, are not comparable to the land involved in this case and, hence,
no reliance can be placed on these instances.
11. Before we analyse the submissions made hereinabove, it will be beneficial to delve upon the Report dated 15102008 submitted by the Court Commissioner.
The report provided an appraisal of appellants land and the possibility of utilizing it for commercial purpose or residential purpose.
The Report (relevant extract only) reads as follows: The acquired properties are situated in Paloliparam town which is part of Vadakara town and is adjacent to Karimbanapalam town also.
All the acquired properties are having good commercial and industrial importance.
There are so many shops businesses, workshops.

Rural Superintendent of Office, DYSP Office, Passport Cell, Narcotic Cell, PWD Office, PWD Quarters, Post Office, Govt. Ayurveda Hospital, Calicut University Centre,
B.Ed College , M.B.A. College, Municipal Market building, Kerala Dinesh Beedi Factory, Vadakara Coop. Rural Bank Branch, UP School and High School, Temples, Mosque etc., adjacent to acquired properties.
The distance from old and new bus stands to acquired properties as also in the unacquired properties.
Shop buildings acquired are being demolished at the time of inspection.
I am herewith submitting a sketch which may be treated as part of this report.
12. It goes without saying that the acquired land of the appellants appears to be located almost in the heart of the township, which is surrounded by developed areas and abuts the National Highway.
Given this geographic fact, the land appears to have the capacity to be utilized for any public purpose including residential or commercial.
A similar point can be made regarding the condition of the land acquired vide the Award in Exhibit `A2.
While the land of the appellants is located on the eastern side of the National Highway, the land involved in Exhibit `A2 falls on the western side of the National Highway.

True that both the parcels of land were not contiguous, yet their commercial potentiality and future utility will be nearly the same, as they are within the municipal limits and abutting the National Highway.

Even if we accept the reasoning assigned by the High Court that the property in Exhibit `A2 was slightly superior in quality, it cannot be overlooked that the said land was acquired in the year 2002, whereas the land of the appellants came to be acquired after 2 years and 4 months in the year 2005.

Applying broadly the principle of annual escalation, it appears to us that the land of the appellants cannot be held to be inferior in any manner for the purpose of grant of compensation, when compared to the property in Exhibit `A2.
13.

We are, however, in agreement with the learned High Court as well as learned State counsel that Exhibit `A1 is a stray instance where Reliance may have offered more than the market price of the land, with a view to capitalize on the small piece of land that was available for its commercial venture to install mobile phone towers.
Thus, it may not be advisable to rely upon Exhibit `A1 to determine the market value of the land that was held by the appellants.

14. In light of the above discussion, we hold that the appellants are entitled to the same rate of compensation as was awarded for the properties acquired vide award Exhibit `A2, i.e., Rs.50,000/
per cent.

sentences.text: For these reasons, we allow the appeal in part and modify the impugned Judgment of the High Court dated 03062010 to the extent that the appellants are held entitled to compensation at Rs.50,000/ per cent for their entire acquired land.

16. Ordered accordingly.
17.

The additional amount of compensation shall be deposited with the Reference Court within eight weeks from today along with interest and other statutory benefits under the Act, and the same shall be released to the appellants without any delay.
J (SURYA KANT) J (J.K. MAHESHWARI)
NEW DELHI 16TH MARCH, 2023.
